Kenny Boyd (reviewer on the Baylor Athletics Software and Technology Management
Framework) consistently pushes back on three things in draft policy language:

1. **No language that implies the department was previously incompetent.** He cut
   "so the department stops discovering it is in the final year of an agreement
   with no time to act" for exactly this reason. Rewrite as forward-looking
   capability ("advance visibility of contract end dates and the lead time to
   evaluate options"), not as a problem being fixed.
2. **No judgmental or ranking-flavored labels.** He rejected the Light / Standard /
   Elevated review tiers. Neutral, descriptive, escalating names work better —
   Level 1 Standard / Level 2 Enhanced / Level 3 Comprehensive Review. He floated
   Basic / Intermediate / Advanced, which reads as sophistication of the
   *technology* rather than depth of *review*.
3. **Name the seniority of the reviewer, not just the office.** For ITS he wanted
   it clear that a supervisory-level person with authority to commit resources is
   involved, not a line technician. Frame this as decision authority the request
   requires, never as competence of the staff.

He also wants Baylor branding carried through headers/footers and draft status
marked on every page.

**Why:** These are tone constraints, not content ones — the same facts land or
fail on phrasing. Getting them wrong costs a full review cycle.

**How to apply:** Before sending any Athletics policy or framework draft for his
review, scan for blame-implying rationale, ranking adjectives on process tiers,
and unqualified office names where seniority matters.

# Teams plan: Software & Technology Review group

Draft, 2026-10-01. Source: Kenny's 10-01 meeting (KB_TechReview_Followup, 20:43-24:30) and
his follow-up email. Kenny asked Eric to "set up where you feel like we want this
centralized" and then communicate out to the group; Eric chose Teams because it is built
for communication and the files sit on SharePoint underneath. Eric's post is Kenny's cue to
send his own introductory email asking the group to start entering information.

## Goal

One private place where a small group fills in annual cost and use agreement term dates for
the department's 184 products, so Kenny can take a summary to ET before the end of November
and use it in FY28 budget planning. The dollar figures must not reach the wider department.

## Who is in it

| Role | People | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Owners | Kenny Boyd, Eric Rash | Kenny sponsors; Eric runs the workbook and the group |
| Members | CR, CRS, KF | Named in Kenny's email |
| Members, Business Office | Cody, Chris, Erin Boyette, Jovan, Callie | Hold the contract and payment records; Kenny said start with Cody, Chris and Erin |

Nobody else. No guests. Confirm full names for CR, CRS and KF with Kenny before inviting.

## Structure: keep it small

One **private team**, not a channel inside an existing team. A private team keeps the files
private by default; a channel in a department-wide team does not.

- **Name:** Athletics Software & Technology Review
- **Description:** "Annual costs and use agreements for department software. Internal only, for FY28 budget planning."
- **Channels (three):**
  1. **General**: announcements, deadlines, Kenny's updates.
  2. **Costs and Use Agreements**: the workbook, pinned as a tab. Questions about a product go in a reply under that product's name so the history stays findable.
  3. **ET Summary**: the draft report for ET, opened once the costs are mostly in (target early November).

Do not make more channels until a real need appears. ITS approvals (Vault, VALD, Databricks)
stay in Eric's weekly tracker with Kenny, not here: different audience.

## Settings

- Privacy: **Private**. Only owners can add members (Team settings > Member permissions: untick "Allow members to add and remove members").
- Turn off guest access.
- Ask ITS whether Baylor has a sensitivity label (for example "Confidential") for Teams; if so, apply it.
- Files: upload the workbook to the Costs and Use Agreements channel's Files, then **+ Add a tab > Excel** to pin it. Everyone edits the same copy in Excel for the web; no emailed copies.
- After the upload, the Teams copy is the only working copy. Rename the Drive copy in `01_Working/` with `_archive` so nobody edits two versions, and update the row in `docs/STATUS.md` > Where everything lives.

## Build steps (about 30 minutes)

1. Teams > Join or create a team > Create team > From scratch > Private. Name and description as above. (5 min)
2. Add Kenny as a second owner; add the members above. (5 min)
3. Settings: member permissions, guest access. (3 min)
4. Create the two extra channels. (2 min)
5. Upload `Tech_Inventory_COSTS_INTERNAL_ER_2026-10-01.xlsx` to Costs and Use Agreements; pin it as a tab. Open it once in the browser to check the dropdowns and the Summary sheet work. (10 min)
6. Upload the final inventory documents (EXEC_SUMMARY and BY_UNIT, dated 2026-10-01) to General > Files as reference. (2 min)
7. Post the welcome message below in General. (3 min)
8. Tell Kenny the team is live, so he can send his introductory email.

## Welcome post (draft)

> **Welcome to the Software & Technology Review**
>
> Kenny has asked this group to help put annual costs and use agreement dates against the
> department's software and technology, for FY28 budget planning and a summary for ET
> before the end of November.
>
> The workbook is pinned in **Costs and Use Agreements**. It lists all 184 products from
> this fall's inventory (final as of October 1). For each one, please fill in what you know:
> annual cost, who pays, and when the use agreement ends (for example, Kitman Labs ends
> November 2027). Blanks are fine. "Unknown" is better than a guess. Put your initials and
> the date on any row you change.
>
> The **Summary** sheet totals itself as rows are filled in.
>
> This is internal only. Please do not download, forward or share the figures outside this
> team. Questions go in the Costs and Use Agreements channel or straight to me.
>
> Target: as many rows as possible by **October 31**.

## Timeline

| When | What | Who |
|---|---|---|
| Week of Oct 6 | Team live, welcome post, Kenny's intro email | ER, KB |
| Oct 6 to Oct 31 | Fill costs and terms; Erin's CSV merged in | Business Office, group |
| Weekly | Progress number from the Summary sheet in the check-in with Kenny | ER |
| Nov 3 to Nov 14 | Draft ET summary in the ET Summary channel | ER, KB |
| Before Nov 30 | ET summary delivered | KB |

## Open questions for Kenny

- Full names behind CR, CRS and KF.
- Does Baylor's fiscal year start June 1? The workbook assumes so (FY28 = June 2027 to May 2028); the Business Office can change one cell.
- Should Kenny or Eric own the team long term?
- Is October 31 the right target for the costs?

entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_Fireflies__fireflies_get_transcript
entries.description: Fetches detailed meeting transcript by ID, with optional field filtering. Returns transcript content (sentences, speakers) and metadata, but excludes summary data. Each sentence is prefixed with its timestamp range (e.g. "[00:05 - 00:08] Speaker: text") so moments can be anchored back to the recording. To link a user directly to a moment in the meeting, convert the sentence start timestamp to seconds and build a deep link: https://app.fireflies.ai/view/{transcriptId}?t={seconds} (e.g. ?t=441.29 for 07:21). If you need summary data, use fireflies_get_summary instead. If the meeting is currently live (is_live: true), the transcript returned is a point-in-time snapshot of the live transcript with sentences captured so far.

entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_Fireflies__fireflies_search
entries.description:
Advanced search for meeting transcripts using a mini grammar. Supports complex queries with multiple filters.

GRAMMAR SYNTAX:
- keyword:"search term" - Search for keywords in the content. If no scope is specified, the default scope is 'all'.
- scope:title|sentences|all - Define the search scope. Options are 'title', 'sentences', or 'all'. The default is 'all'.
- from:YYYY-MM-DD - Filter meetings from this date (ISO format)
- to:YYYY-MM-DD - Filter meetings until this date (ISO format)
- limit:N - Limit results (max 50)
- skip:N - Skip N results for pagination
- organizers:email1@x.com,email2@x.com - Filter by organizer emails (comma-separated)
- participants:email1@x.com,email2@x.com - Filter by participant emails (comma-separated)
- mine:true|false - Filter to only include user's own meetings
- channel:CHANNEL_ID - Filter meetings by channel/folder ID (use fireflies_list_channels() to find channel IDs)

EXAMPLES:
- "engineering standup" (simple keyword search)
- "keyword:\"performance\" scope:sentences limit:20"
- "channel:64f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1 from:2026-01-01 limit:20"

def col(name):
    return next(i for i, c in enumerate(COLUMNS, 1) if c[0] == name)


def summary(ws, sheet, first, last, categories):
    """Live totals for the ET summary: every figure is a formula over the main sheet,
    so it fills in as the group enters costs and dates."""
    banner(ws, "Software and Technology Review: Summary",
           "Figures update as costs and dates are entered on the Costs and terms sheet. "
           "For FY28 budget planning and the ET summary.", width=4)
    rng = lambda name: "'{}'!${c}${f}:${c}${l}".format(  # noqa: E731
        sheet, c=get_column_letter(col(name)), f=first, l=last)
    cost, term, cat = rng("Annual cost ($)"), rng("Use agreement term end"), rng("Category")
    prod, renew = rng("Product"), rng("Auto-renews?")
    bold, head_fill = Font(name=FONT, bold=True), PatternFill("solid", fgColor=GREEN)
    money = '"$"#,##0.00'
    for c, w in zip("ABCD", (44, 18, 22, 60)):
        ws.column_dimensions[c].width = w

    ws["A5"] = "Fiscal year starts in month (1-12)"
    ws["A5"].font = bold
    ws["B5"] = FY_START_MONTH
    ws["B5"].fill = PatternFill("solid", fgColor=CREAM)
    ws["C5"] = "Assumed June: FY28 = June 2027 to May 2028. Business Office to confirm."
    ws["C5"].font = Font(name=FONT, size=9, italic=True, color=GREY)
    ws.merge_cells("C5:D5")

    def header(r, labels):
        for c, text in enumerate(labels, 1):
            cell = ws.cell(r, c, text)
            cell.font, cell.fill = Font(name=FONT, bold=True, color="FFFFFF"), head_fill

    def put(r, label, value, fmt=None):
        ws.cell(r, 1, label).font = Font(name=FONT, size=10)
        cell = ws.cell(r, 2, value)
        cell.font = Font(name=FONT, size=10, bold=True)
        if fmt:
            cell.number_format = fmt

    header(7, ["Progress", "Value"])
    put(8, "Products listed", f"=COUNTA({prod})")
    put(9, "With an annual cost entered", f"=COUNT({cost})")
    put(10, "Total annual cost entered", f"=SUM({cost})", money)
    put(11, "With a use agreement term end entered", f"=COUNT({term})")
    put(12, "Set to auto-renew", f'=COUNTIF({renew},"Yes")')

    # Start date of fiscal year N (two-digit). With a June start, FY28 starts 2027-06-01.
    fy = lambda n: f"DATE({2000 + n}-IF($B$5>1,1,0),$B$5,1)"  # noqa: E731
    header(14, ["Use agreements ending", "Agreements", "Annual cost of those"])
    lo, hi = FY_ROWS[0], FY_ROWS[-1]
    rows = [(f"FY{lo} or earlier", f'{term},"<"&{fy(lo + 1)}')]
    rows += [(f"FY{n}", f'{term},">="&{fy(n)},{term},"<"&{fy(n + 1)}') for n in FY_ROWS[1:-1]]
    rows += [(f"FY{hi} or later", f'{term},">="&{fy(hi)}')]
    for i, (label, crit) in enumerate(rows, 15):
        put(i, label, f"=COUNTIFS({crit})")
        c = ws.cell(i, 3, f"=SUMIFS({cost},{crit})")
        c.number_format, c.font = money, Font(name=FONT, size=10)
    n = 15 + len(rows)
    put(n, "No term end entered yet", f"=COUNTA({prod})-COUNT({term})")

    header(n + 2, ["Category", "Products", "With a cost", "Annual cost entered"])
    for i, (name, count) in enumerate(categories, n + 3):
        ws.cell(i, 1, name).font = Font(name=FONT, size=10)
        ws.cell(i, 2, f'=COUNTIF({cat},A{i})').font = Font(name=FONT, size=10)
        ws.cell(i, 3, f'=COUNTIFS({cat},A{i},{cost},"<>")').font = Font(name=FONT, size=10)
        c = ws.cell(i, 4, f'=SUMIF({cat},A{i},{cost})')
        c.number_format, c.font = money, Font(name=FONT, size=10)


def guide(ws, n_active, n_retired):
    lines = [
        ("How to fill this in", True),
        ("", False),
        ("Green columns come from the inventory survey. Do not edit them; corrections go to Eric.", False),
        ("Gold columns are for cost and contract details. Fill in as many as you can; blanks are fine.", False),
        ("Annual cost: what the department pays per year. For per-seat or monthly pricing, enter the yearly total and pick the cost basis.", False),
        ("Paid by: the unit or budget line that pays, as the Business Office records it.", False),
        ("Use agreement term end: the date the current contract or subscription ends (for example, Kitman Labs, November 2027). "
         "Notice to cancel: days of notice the vendor needs before that date.", False),
        ("Auto-renews: Yes, No, or Unknown. Unknown is better than a guess.", False),
        ("Notes: anything that matters for FY28 planning (price increase, overlap with another product, plan to drop).", False),
        ("Entered by and Last updated: your initials and the date, on every row you change, so the group can see who confirmed what.", False),
        ("The Summary sheet totals itself from these columns; nothing there needs typing except the fiscal year start month.", False),
        ("", False),
        (f"Products in use or planned: {n_active}. Fully retired in the last 12 months: {n_retired} (own sheet; a contract may still be running). "
         "Products one unit dropped but others still use stay on the main sheet, with a note.", False),
        ("Generic laptops, phones, tablets and printers are left out.", False),
        (f"Product list from the inventory survey export of {long_date(EXPORT)}; collection closed September 29, 2026.", False),
        ("", False),
        (f"Internal only. Shared with: {GROUP}. Do not forward.", True),
    ]
    ws.column_dimensions["A"].width = 120
    for i, (text, bold) in enumerate(lines, 1):
        c = ws.cell(i, 1, text)
        c.font = Font(name=FONT, size=14 if i == 1 else 11, bold=bold, color=GREEN if bold else "000000")
        c.alignment = Alignment(wrap_text=True)


def build():
    active = active_products()
    names = {r[0] for r in active}
    retired = retired_products(names)
    missing = sorted(set(KNOWN) - {r[0] for r in active})
    if missing:
        sys.exit(f"[error] KNOWN entries not in the product list: {', '.join(missing)}")
    wb = Workbook()
    summ = wb.active
    summ.title = "Summary"
    ws = wb.create_sheet("Costs and terms")
    first, last = product_sheet(
        ws, active, "Software and Technology Review: Costs and Use Agreements",
        f"Final product list as of {long_date(TODAY)} ({len(active)} products). "
        "Green columns from the survey; gold columns to fill in. For FY28 budget planning.",
        notes=stopped_notes(names))
    cats = collections.Counter(r[1] for r in active).most_common()
    summary(summ, ws.title, first, last, cats)
    product_sheet(wb.create_sheet("Retired"), retired,
                  "Retired in the last 12 months",
                  "No unit uses these any more; check whether a contract or renewal is still running.")
    guide(wb.create_sheet("How to fill in"), len(active), len(retired))
    os.makedirs(DELIV, exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(DELIV, STEM + ".xlsx")
    if os.path.exists(path):
        sys.exit(f"[error] {path} exists; it may hold filled-in costs. Move it before rebuilding.")
    wb.save(path)
    print(f"wrote {path}: {len(active)} active, {len(retired)} retired")

# Software and Technology Review: How to Use This Team

**Draft, 2026-10-12. Internal only. Do not forward or share outside this team.**

Upload a copy of this page to the **General** channel, under Files, so everyone can find it.

## What this team is for

Kenny Boyd asked us to add a yearly cost and a contract end date to each software product in the department's technology inventory. Kenny will use the totals for FY28 budget planning. A summary goes to ET before November 30.

Blank cells are fine. "Unknown" is better than a guess.

## The three channels

- **General**: announcements, deadlines and updates from Kenny and Eric. Reference files are under Files.
- **Costs and Use Agreements**: the working workbook, pinned as a tab at the top of the channel. Ask questions here. Reply under the product's name so the history stays in one place.
- **ET Summary**: the draft summary for ET. It opens in early November.

## Before you start

1. Open the **Costs and Use Agreements** channel.
2. Open the workbook from the pinned tab. Use Excel for the web. Do not download a copy or email one. Everyone edits the same file.
3. Read the **How to fill in** tab. It is the short version of this page.

## The workbook has four tabs

| Tab | What it is | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| How to fill in | The rules for the sheet | Read only |
| Summary | Totals that update by themselves: products listed, cost entered, agreements ending by fiscal year, totals by category | Read only. The one exception is the fiscal year start month in cell B5. |
| Costs and terms | The main sheet. One row per product, 184 products. | Fill in the gold columns. |
| Retired | Products that no unit uses any more | Check whether a contract is still running. |

## The columns

**Green columns** come from the inventory survey. Do not edit them. If one looks wrong, tell Eric.

**Gold columns** are yours to fill in:

- **Annual cost ($)**: what the department pays each year. For a monthly or per-seat price, enter the yearly total and pick the Cost basis.
- **Cost basis**: pick from the list.
- **Paid by (unit / budget)**: the unit or budget line that pays, as the Business Office records it.
- **Use agreement start**: the date the current contract or subscription started.
- **Use agreement term end**: the date the current contract or subscription ends. Example: Kitman Labs, November 2027.
- **Auto-renews?**: Yes, No or Unknown.
- **Notice to cancel (days)**: the number of days' notice the vendor needs before the term end.
- **Vendor contact**: the vendor contact's name or email, if you know it.
- **Notes**: anything that matters for FY28 planning, such as a price increase, an overlap with another product, or a plan to drop it.
- **Entered by (initials)** and **Last updated**: your initials and today's date on every row you change. This lets the group see who confirmed what.

## How to fill in one row

1. Find the product in the **Product** column.
2. Enter what you know. Skip what you do not know.
3. Add your initials and today's date.
4. If you have a question, reply in the channel under the product's name.

## Rules of the road

- Do not add, delete or move rows. Do not change the Product or Category columns.
- Sorting and filtering are fine. Sort the whole table, not one column, so rows stay together.
- Do not download, print, screenshot, forward or share the figures.
- Do not add people to this team. Eric and Kenny manage membership.
- Generic laptops, phones, tablets and printers are not on the list. That is on purpose.

## Timeline

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Oct 6 to Oct 31 | Fill in costs and terms as far as you can. |
| Weekly | Eric checks the progress count on the Summary tab. |
| Nov 3 to Nov 14 | Eric drafts the ET summary in the ET Summary channel. |
| Before Nov 30 | Kenny delivers the ET summary. |

Target for costs: **October 31**.

## Questions

Ask in the **Costs and Use Agreements** channel, or message Eric Rash directly.

- **Eric Rash**: runs the workbook and this team.
- **Kenny Boyd**: sponsors the review.

# Teams plan: Software & Technology Review group

Draft, 2026-10-01. Source: Kenny's 10-01 meeting (KB_TechReview_Followup, 20:43-24:30) and
his follow-up email. Kenny asked Eric to "set up where you feel like we want this
centralized" and then communicate out to the group; Eric chose Teams because it is built
for communication and the files sit on SharePoint underneath. Eric's post is Kenny's cue to
send his own introductory email asking the group to start entering information.

## Goal

One private place where a small group fills in annual cost and use agreement term dates for
the department's 184 products, so Kenny can take a summary to ET before the end of November
and use it in FY28 budget planning. The dollar figures must not reach the wider department.

## Who is in it

| Role | People | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Owners | Kenny Boyd, Eric Rash | Kenny sponsors; Eric runs the workbook and the group |
| Members | CR, CRS, KF | Named in Kenny's email |
| Members, Business Office | Cody, Chris, Erin Boyette, Jovan, Callie | Hold the contract and payment records; Kenny said start with Cody, Chris and Erin |

Nobody else. No guests. Confirm full names for CR, CRS and KF with Kenny before inviting.

## Structure: keep it small

One **private team**, not a channel inside an existing team. A private team keeps the files
private by default; a channel in a department-wide team does not.

- **Name:** Athletics Software & Technology Review
- **Description:** "Annual costs and use agreements for department software. Internal only, for FY28 budget planning."
- **Channels (three):**
  1. **General**: announcements, deadlines, Kenny's updates.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- **Registry drift.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It compares `portfolio.json` with every DEV folder and Drive `01_PROJECTS` folder and only reports; it never moves anything. Do not fix drift during closeout. List each item it found under "Still open", naming any folder created this session first: that is a project started without a row, the exact way projects got lost before the 2026-10-03 organization pass. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran; say so, do not call it clean. Cowork cannot run it; say it was skipped.
- **7-day rule.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply`. Name any project it paused, and any project on its last two days, under "Still open" with what it still needs (a receiver, step 1). Revive with the board's status pill or `portfolio.py` once there is a first step to show.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- **Registry edits get their own commit.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json` shows a change (board edits from the day, `set-status`, `set-receiver`), commit that file alone first as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`, then the rest. The board header's "N unpushed registry edits" counts these; a skipped one becomes a JSON merge conflict when the other machine edits too.
- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- If `~/.claude/mods` changed this session (a mod added, edited or `.disabled`), run the mods sync (`bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` on the Mac, `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` on Windows) and list any invalid mod under "Still open".
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to open), not a theme: it is the line `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows Eric the next morning
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric, each one written out in full as its own top-level bullet: the question itself and enough context to answer it without opening another file. Never a pointer ("See PLAN.md"): `/startup` reads this section across every repo with `where-was-i.py --decisions`, and a pointer gives no question to answer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …` or strike them through (`~~…~~`) so they drop off that list. Leave the section empty, not "-", when nothing is waiting.
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

Then run `python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 1`. It prints exactly what tomorrow's `/startup` will show as "Decisions waiting on you". Every decision this session left open must appear there as a readable question; if one is missing or shows as a pointer, fix that repo's `## Open questions` before the commit.

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

**Keep the resume cards true (PM system design Decision 9).** The live board shows each project as a card read from STATUS and the registry; if a card doesn't make sense tonight, it won't in six weeks. Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (about a minute), then `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. It prints the card of every registry project touched today, on either machine, with its gaps. Fix each gap before the Step 2 commit:

- `STATUS has no entry dated <today>`: add `- <today>: <what happened>` under the repo's Done / Current state.
- `STATUS has no Next item`: put one concrete action first under `## Next`.
- `no next step (next_action)` (Drive-only row): set it on the board or with `portfolio.py add-update <name> "<note>" --next-action "<step>"`.
- `needs a receiver`: `portfolio.py set-receiver <name> "<who>"` (a name, or `me: <why>`). Ask Eric when it is not obvious from the session; never invent one.
- `touched but marked <status>`: revive it (`portfolio.py set-status <name> active`) or say in STATUS why a retired project was touched.

Re-run `card-check` after the fixes. Its output is the last section of the report (**Cards:**); trim to projects with work today if it is long, but never drop one that still has a gap.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Registry drift:** <N items, or "none"> (`portfolio.py crosswalk`)
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.

**Cards:** <`portfolio.py card-check` output, after the Step 4 fixes>
```

The cards come last on purpose: they are what the next session, on either machine, picks up from.

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

**Where everything landed.** Build that list from the ledger, not from memory: the Step 4 `landed.py scan --days 1` already refreshed it (it reads git in every DEV repo and file times on Drive and the vault, so files written by scripts and shell copies are included); run `landed.py show --days 1`. Put its project-grouped output in the report under **Landed:** (trim to the projects this session touched if it is long). The ledger lives in `~/.claude/global-memory/landed/` and is pushed with global-memory, so `/landed` on the other machine shows it too.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.
